articles.title: Gazans face near-daily Israeli strikes a year into ceasefire
articles.summary: The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for the remaining hostages held in Gaza.
articles.body:
More than 1,400 people in Gaza have been killed in Israeli attacks since the start of the ceasefire on 10 October last year, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

The ceasefire saw thousands of Palestinians held by Israel released in return for the remaining hostages held in Gaza.

It was an agreement to end the war, triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 taken hostage.

But even during the ceasefire, Israel has continued launching strikes in Gaza almost every day.

Israel says it is targeting Hamas operatives and accuses Hamas of continued violations of the ceasefire.

The total death toll from Israeli attacks since the start of the war in Gaza now stands at more than 74,000, according to the Gaza health ministry.

articles.summary: Inscrições custam R$ 30 e ficam abertas até o dia 31 de outubro. Provas estão previstas para ocorrer no dia 7 de novembro.
articles.body:
Universidade divulgou edital para preenchimento de vagas — Foto: Cícero Oliveira/UFRN

A Escola de Saúde da UFRN (ESUFRN) abriu nesta quarta-feira (7) inscrições para um processo seletivo com 252 vagas em cursos técnicos gratuitos . O ingresso acontece no ano de 2027.

As oportunidades são para Técnico em Agente Comunitário de Saúde, Técnico em Cuidados de Idosos, Técnico em Enfermagem, Técnico em Terapias Holísticas e Técnico em Vigilância em Saúde (veja de forma detalhada mais abaixo).

As inscrições ficam abertas até o dia 21 de outubro pelo site comperve.ufrn.br, na aba Cursos Técnicos. A taxa de inscrição é de R$ 30, com possibilidade de isenção para candidatos que atendam aos critérios estabelecidos no edital.

Os cursos, no entanto, são gratuitos e não há cobrança de mensalidades.

A seleção dos candidatos ocorre por meio de prova, que está prevista para acontecer no dia 7 de novembro, às 14h, em Natal .

Os cursos são na modalidade presencial, com aulas na sede da Escola de Saúde, localizada no campus central da UFRN, em Natal.

articles.title: Casal é condenado após esconder drogas em pousada em Pipa | G1
articles.standfirst: Homem e mulher foram condenados a 11 anos, 9 meses e 22 dias de prisão por tráfico e associação para o tráfico; polícia apreendeu 173 porções de drogas no local.
articles.summary: Casal foi condenado por tráfico e associação após polícia encontrar 173 porções de drogas em quarto de pousada na Praia de Pipa, no RN.
articles.body:
Um casal foi condenado pelos crimes de tráfico de drogas e associação para o tráfico após uma ação policial em uma pousada na Praia da Pipa, em Tibau do Sul , no litoral Sul do Rio Grande do Norte. A decisão foi proferida pela 1ª Vara da Comarca de Goianinha.

De acordo com a denúncia do Ministério Público do Rio Grande do Norte (MPRN), os dois estavam no quarto da pousada quando foram presos. Durante a ação, os policiais apreenderam 115 porções de maconha e 58 de cocaína, além de uma arma de fogo, dinheiro, duas balanças de precisão, embalagens do tipo "zip lock" e uma caderneta com anotações relacionadas ao fluxo financeiro da venda de drogas.

Segundo o MP, o casal havia se estabelecido na Praia de Pipa com a finalidade de realizar o tráfico. A denúncia aponta que o homem atuava na organização logística da atividade, no armazenamento das drogas e na segurança do ponto de venda. A mulher, por sua vez, seria responsável pela contabilidade e pelo controle financeiro.

O revólver encontrado no quarto da pousada estava carregado com nove munições. Para o Ministério Público, a arma seria utilizada para a segurança dos acusados.

As defesas dos dois acusados alegaram que as provas deveriam ser consideradas ilegais porque os policiais entraram no quarto da pousada sem mandado judicial. Segundo os advogados, não havia situação de flagrante nem justificativa para afastar a proteção constitucional do domicílio.

O juiz Marck Clark Santiago rejeitou o argumento. Na sentença, ele reconheceu que o quarto de pousada é protegido pela garantia constitucional de inviolabilidade do domicílio, mas considerou que a entrada dos policiais foi precedida por uma investigação.

“No caso concreto, a prova produzida em juízo demonstra que a atuação policial não decorreu de mera intuição, denúncia anônima desacompanhada de diligências preliminares ou de abordagem aleatória.”

Segundo o magistrado, os policiais já investigavam o homem havia semanas. Ainda conforme a sentença, ele era apontado como integrante de uma organização criminosa que atuava na região de Tibau do Sul e também era investigado por possível participação em um homicídio ocorrido dias antes da prisão.

Os policiais relataram que o homem já havia conseguido fugir de uma ação anterior. Para o juiz, as circunstâncias demonstraram que a diligência foi baseada em elementos obtidos durante a investigação.

Em relação à mulher, a defesa alegou que ela estava na pousada apenas por causa do relacionamento com o homem. O juiz, no entanto, entendeu que as provas apontavam para uma participação direta na atividade criminosa.

A caderneta apreendida no quarto foi considerada uma das provas da atuação dela. Segundo a sentença, depoimentos atribuíram à mulher a função de registrar e controlar a comercialização das drogas.

“Sua atuação, portanto, não se limitava à presença física no ambiente, mas integrava a execução do delito mediante colaboração material na guarda, fracionamento e organização da mercancia ilícita”, escreveu o magistrado.

Para a Justiça, a quantidade de drogas, o fracionamento dos entorpecentes e a presença de materiais utilizados na comercialização comprovaram a materialidade e a autoria dos crimes.

O homem foi condenado a 11 anos, nove meses e 22 dias de reclusão, além do pagamento de 1.538 dias-multa. A pena deverá ser cumprida inicialmente em regime fechado, e ele não poderá recorrer em liberdade.

A mulher recebeu a mesma pena de 11 anos, nove meses e 22 dias de reclusão, além dos 1.538 dias-multa. A diferença é que ela poderá recorrer em liberdade e cumprir a pena em prisão domiciliar por ser mãe de uma criança menor de 12 anos.

articles.title: Poliana Rocha se surpreende ao se deparar com mudança de Zé Felipe | G1
articles.standfirst: O filho do cantor Leonardo está passando uma temporada nos Estados Unidos para um novo projeto musical. No vídeo, é possível ver caixas empilhadas e até um equipamento de academia.
articles.summary: O filho do cantor Leonardo está passando uma temporada nos Estados Unidos para um novo projeto musical. No vídeo, é possível ver caixas empilhadas e até um equipamento de academia.
articles.body:
Poliana Rocha, esposa de Leonardo , se surpreendeu ao chegar de viagem e se deparar com a "mudança" do filho Zé Felipe na sala de sua casa, em Goiânia (veja o vídeo acima) . O cantor está passando uma temporada nos Estados Unidos para um novo projeto musical e deixou alguns pertences na casa dos pais.

"O que a que a gente não faz por filho", disse ela.

O vídeo foi publicado por Poliana nesta quarta-feira (8). Nos últimos dias ela e o marido, o cantor Leonardo, estavam em viagem pela Europa. A influenciadora foi surpreendida ao chegar em casa e encontrar os pertences do filho embrulhados em caixas em alguns cômodos da sala.

Ao mostrar os espaços, ela explicou que Zé Felipe ficará fora do Brasil por algum tempo, trabalhando em um projeto de música country, e enviou a mudança para lá. "A casa está daquele modelo" , brincou.

Poliana Rocha se surpreende ao chegar em casa e se deparar com mudança de Zé Felipe na sala — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram de Poliana Rocha

Nas últimas semanas, Poliana e Leonardo dividiram com os fãs e seguidores alguns registros da viagem a Paris, na França. Os passeios renderam momentos divertidos na web, como um vídeo do cantor segurando uma garrafa gigante em um restaurante na capital francesa.

A brincadeira aconteceu tempos depois de Poliana revelar ao público que o marido iria ficar 30 dias sem beber. A decisão foi tomada depois que foram identificadas alterações em taxas de exames do cantor.

"30 dias sem beber nada de bebida alcoólica, realmente pra mim foi um motivo de muito sofrimento. A vontade até de chorar, juro por Deus. Uma pessoa igual eu, acostumado igual caranguejo de laboratório, só no álcool. 30 dias não foi brincadeira não, gente", declarou Leonardo enquanto pegava uma taça com uma bebida.

articles.title: Rodovia Fernão Dias terá interdições em Vargem nesta quinta (8) | G1
articles.standfirst: Bloqueios acontecem nos dois sentidos da rodovia durante içamento de pilares e preparação para instalação de nova estrutura.
articles.summary: A Rodovia Fernão Dias tem bloqueios nos dois sentidos nesta quinta para obras na passarela de Vargem, estrutura que desabou e causou mortes em agosto.
articles.body:
No interior de SP, queda de passarela provocou duas mortes na Rodovia Fernão Dias em agosto - imagem de arquivo. — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A Rodovia Fernão Dias terá alterações no trânsito nesta quinta-feira (8) para as obras de reconstrução da passarela que desabou em agosto , em Vargem , no interior de São Paulo.

Durante a manhã, será feito o içamento de um pilar na pista sentido São Paulo. Durante a operação, o acesso à Rua Fernando Berardi, no Centro da cidade, ficará temporariamente bloqueado.

À tarde, os trabalhos continuam com o içamento de outro pilar, desta vez na pista sentido Belo Horizonte.

Já à noite, entre 21h e 2h, a faixa da esquerda será interditada nos dois sentidos da rodovia para a preparação do lançamento da viga da nova passarela. Durante esse período, o trânsito vai fluir apenas pela faixa da direita em cada sentido.

A passarela que está sendo reconstruída desabou em agosto, após ser atingida por um caminhão. Duas pessoas morreram e uma ficou ferida no acidente.

A estrutura caiu sobre a rodovia, atingindo veículos que passavam pelo trecho - relembre clicando aqui.

articles.title: Can emergency reserves ease the diesel crisis?
articles.summary: The G7 plans to release emergency fuel stocks as diesel shortages raise transport costs and squeeze household budgets.
articles.body:
From delivering goods to harvesting crops, much of the world’s economic activity depends on diesel fuel.

When it becomes scarce or expensive, the impact reaches far beyond the pump to food prices, household budgets and economic growth.

Right now, prices have hit record highs.

Supply has tightened as the United States-Israel war on Iran disrupts shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Ukrainian attacks damage Russian refineries and China reportedly curbs its exports.

The Group of Seven has agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel from its emergency stockpiles over four months. That amount equates to about one day of global oil demand.

articles.summary: Feriado nacional provoca mudança de horário em centro de compras e serviços da Capital do Agreste.
articles.body:
Feriado de Nossa Senhora Aparecida provoca mudanças em horários de serviços e comércios de Caruaru — Foto: Edivaldo Coelho / TV Asa Branca

Na próxima segunda-feira (12), é celebrado o dia de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, padroeira do Brasil. Por causa do feriado, alguns estabelecimentos e serviços terão mudanças no funcionamento.

O comércio de rua poderá funcionar normalmente nas lojas que solicitaram ao sindicato. Centro de compras também estarão abertos. Alguns serviços não irão funcionar.

Confira o que abre e fecha em Caruaru no feriado:

Comércio de rua : De acordo com o Sindicato dos Lojistas do Comércio de Caruaru, as empresas que cumprirem as regras poderão funcionar normalmente.

Caruaru Shopping : O centro de compras do bairro Indianópolis irá funcionar em horário especial. Lojas, quiosques e serviços abrem de 10h às 22h. A academia irá funcionar em horário reduzido, de 7h às 19h. A praça de alimentação abre de 1hh e fecha às 22h. O supermercado e as áreas de lazer funcionam no horário normal. Os cinemas funcionam de acordo com o horário da sessão.

Shopping Difusora : O centeo de compras do bairro Maurício de Nassau vai funcionar em horário especial. As lojas e os quiosques irão abrir das 11h às 20h. Já a praça de alimentação e lazer segue o mesmo o horário. O cinema irá funcionar conforme a programação própria.

Bancos : Segundo a Febraban, os bancos estarão fechados no feriado.

Correios : Os correios terão as agências fechadas no feriado.

A próxima oportunidade de folga será em 28 de outubro, Dia do Servidor Público. A data é considerada ponto facultativo no âmbito federal.

➡️ Na prática, estados e municípios podem adotar a data em seus próprios calendários como feriado, conforme regulamentação local, o que pode abrir espaço para uma emenda e prolongar o descanso.

Depois disso, novembro chega com três feriados nacionais. O primeiro deles será em 2 de novembro, Dia de Finados.

O feriado cairá novamente em uma segunda-feira, o que permitirá três dias seguidos de descanso para os trabalhadores que folgam aos fins de semana.

Quem for escalado para trabalhar no feriado terá direito, em regra, ao pagamento em dobro ou a uma folga compensatória.

articles.title: Carro avança sinal vermelho e bate em outro veículo na Avenida Colares Moreira, em São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Com o impacto, os dois carros ficaram danificados e um dos motoristas sofreu arranhões. Acidente também bloqueou a faixa exclusiva de ônibus e o acesso a um retorno da avenida.
articles.summary: Com o impacto, os dois carros ficaram danificados e um dos motoristas sofreu arranhões. Acidente também bloqueou a faixa exclusiva de ônibus e o acesso a um retorno da avenida.
articles.body:
Um acidente envolvendo dois carros foi registrado na manhã desta quinta-feira (8), na Avenida Colares Moreira, no sentido Renascença–São Francisco, em São Luís . Um carro preto avançou o sinal vermelho e atingiu a lateral de um carro prata.

Com o impacto da batida, os dois veículos ficaram danificados. O motorista do carro atingido sofreu arranhões e relatou que o uso do cinto de segurança foi fundamental para protegê-lo durante a colisão.

Após o acidente, o carro prata ficou parado na entrada de um retorno de quadra, impedindo o acesso de outros veículos. Já o carro preto ficou na faixa exclusiva de ônibus da avenida, bloqueando a passagem dos coletivos.

Equipes da Secretaria Municipal de Trânsito e Transportes (SMTT) estiveram no local para acompanhar a ocorrência.

articles.title: Mães protestam após roda se soltar de ônibus escolar em MS  | G1
articles.standfirst: As mães fizeram manifestação em frente à Escola Estadual Nova Itamarati nesta quinta-feira (8). A prefeitura anunciou vistoria nos 26 ônibus da empresa responsável pelo transporte.
articles.summary: As mães fizeram manifestação em frente à Escola Estadual Nova Itamarati nesta quinta-feira (8). A prefeitura anunciou vistoria nos 26 ônibus da empresa responsável pelo transporte.
articles.body:
Mães de estudantes da região de Itamarati, em Ponta Porã , a 324 km de Campo Grande, fizeram um protesto na manhã desta quinta-feira (8) para cobrar melhorias no transporte escolar. A manifestação ocorreu dois dias após a roda de um ônibus se soltar durante o trajeto pela MS-164 e assustar os alunos.

Com cartazes, as famílias cobraram mais segurança para os estudantes. Um dos cartazes levados ao protesto dizia:

“Queremos melhoria nos ônibus e mais segurança para os nossos filhos”.

O caso da roda que se soltou ocorreu na terça-feira (6). Segundo relatos de mães e estudantes, o problema aumentou a preocupação das famílias, que já afirmavam enfrentar falhas frequentes nos veículos usados no transporte escolar da região.

Após o episódio, a Prefeitura de Ponta Porã retirou o ônibus envolvido de circulação e abriu um procedimento administrativo contra a empresa responsável pelo serviço. Segundo o município, o processo está na fase final e pode resultar na rescisão do contrato e na aplicação de penalidades, com garantia de defesa à empresa.

Mães protestam em frente a escola onde os filhos estudam. — Foto: Liniker Ribeiro

A empresa responsável pelo transporte escolar possui contrato com a Prefeitura de Ponta Porã desde 2023 e atende 26 linhas. Deste total, 18 ficam na região do Itamarati.

Segundo a prefeitura, os 26 ônibus estão vinculados às respectivas linhas e o veículo envolvido no incidente permanece fora de circulação.

O município informou que, há pouco mais de 30 dias, a empresa apresentou um laudo técnico que atestava a regularidade e a segurança dos veículos. Após o incidente, a prefeitura determinou uma nova vistoria em toda a frota.

A inspeção será feita por uma comissão da Secretaria Municipal de Educação, com apoio de mecânicos. A previsão é que a vistoria ocorra nesta quinta-feira (8), já que não houve aula e os ônibus não estavam em operação.

Segundo a prefeitura, a análise também vai verificar se os veículos que circulam correspondem aos que aparecem no laudo apresentado pela empresa. Qualquer ônibus que apresente irregularidade será retirado de circulação.

O município também abriu um procedimento para uma contratação emergencial de veículos caso a vistoria identifique ônibus fora das condições exigidas.

Segundo a prefeitura, o processo segue os trâmites legais e não permite uma substituição imediata de toda a frota. Caso o contrato atual seja rescindido, a empresa será substituída conforme a legislação.

A Prefeitura informou que a fiscalização do transporte escolar fica sob responsabilidade da Secretaria Municipal de Educação, por meio dos fiscais do contrato. O documento prevê o acompanhamento dos serviços e a realização de vistorias nos veículos.

Segundo o município, reclamações anteriores foram analisadas e, nos casos em que foram confirmados problemas, a empresa recebeu notificações e realizou as correções solicitadas.

Após o episódio desta semana, a prefeitura afirma que vai intensificar a fiscalização, com vistorias próprias em intervalos menores e acompanhamento das condições dos ônibus, dos registros de manutenção e da execução do contrato.

O procedimento administrativo contra a empresa deve ser concluído nos próximos dias. A prefeitura informou que não vai antecipar a conclusão das análises técnicas e administrativas antes do encerramento do processo.

articles.title: Deputados mais votados de SP somam 18 milhões de seguidores e adotam estratégias diferentes de campanha | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento considera seis candidatos eleitos com mais de 500 mil votos, que somam mais de 18 milhões de seguidores, com audiências construídas antes da campanha. Gastos revelam estratégias diferentes para transformar seguidores em circulação política.
articles.summary: Levantamento considera seis candidatos eleitos com mais de 500 mil votos, que somam mais de 18 milhões de seguidores, com audiências construídas antes da campanha. Gastos revelam estratégias diferentes para transformar seguidores em circulação política.
articles.body:
Da esquerda para a direita: Lucas Pavanato, Erika Hilton, Eduarda Campopiano, Sâmia Bomfim, Kim Kataguiri e Eduardo Suplicy. — Foto: Reprodução

Os seis candidatos a deputado estadual e federal mais votados de São Paulo , com mais de 500 mil votos nas eleições deste ano, chegaram às urnas com uma audiência digital de milhões de pessoas. Juntos, Lucas Pavanato (PL), Erika Hilton (PSOL), Eduarda Campopiano (PL), Eduardo Suplicy (PT), Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL) e Kim Kataguiri (Missão) somam mais de 18 milhões de seguidores no Instagram.

As prestações de contas ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) mostram, porém, que eles usaram essa audiência de maneiras diferentes (leia mais abaixo).

Pavanato e Campopiano, os dois mais votados do grupo, destinaram metade ou mais das despesas de campanha ao digital. Já Erika Hilton e Sâmia Bomfim, que também têm milhões de seguidores, gastaram parcelas maiores com material gráfico.

Para especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 , a quantidade de seguidores não equivale ao número de votos, mas pode representar um ativo político construído antes da eleição. Ou seja, uma audiência capaz de receber, compartilhar e fazer circular conteúdos.

Lucas Pavanato foi o candidato mais votado entre os seis, com 3.038.438 votos. Sua campanha declarou R$ 2,7 milhões em despesas, dos quais cerca de R$ 1,35 milhão — 50% do total — foi destinado a impulsionamento, comunicação digital e produção de conteúdo. Outros R$ 352.500 (13%) foram usados em materiais impressos.

O candidato do PL chegou à eleição com cerca de 5,5 milhões de seguidores no Instagram.

Eduarda Campopiano (PL), segunda mais votada, recebeu 1.956.238 votos. A deputada estadual eleita declarou R$ 654 mil em despesas, sendo cerca de R$ 400 mil, ou 61,1%, destinados à comunicação digital. Ela tinha aproximadamente 2,5 milhões de seguidores e fez uma campanha conjunta com Pavanato.

Nos dois casos, o investimento durante a campanha se somou a uma audiência que já havia sido construída anteriormente .

Para a cientista política Tathiana Chicarino, coordenadora do curso de Sociologia e Política da Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo (FESP-SP), essa construção é parte de uma transformação mais ampla da política.

“As redes sociais não se consolidaram como um dos principais espaços na disputa eleitoral. Isso se configura na nossa vida. Então, as redes sociais são um espaço importante da nossa sociabilidade", afirma.

Segundo ela, a transformação é parte de um processo mais amplo de digitalização da vida, que começou antes da pandemia e alterou também a maneira como as pessoas recebem informação, trabalham, estudam, se relacionam e consomem entretenimento.

“O que acontece é uma digitalização da vida, que se acelera bastante com a pandemia, mas que já vinha acontecendo desde os anos 2000, 2010.”

A deputada federal Érika Hilton (PSOL) e o vereador Lucas Pavanato (PL). — Foto: Montagem/g1/Reprodução/Agência Câmara e Rede Câmara

A presença digital, porém, não é exclusividade dos candidatos que mais gastaram nas redes.

Erika Hilton foi a segunda deputada federal mais votada do estado, com 1.596.383 votos. Ela declarou R$ 1,63 milhão em despesas de campanha. Cerca de R$ 188 mil, ou 11,5% do total, foram destinados a comunicação digital e impulsionamento, enquanto aproximadamente R$ 453 mil, ou 27,8%, foram gastos com material gráfico.

A deputada tem cerca de 5,3 milhões de seguidores no Instagram, uma audiência maior que a de Pavanato e mais que o dobro da de Campopiano.

Sâmia Bomfim (PSOL) recebeu 583.107 votos e declarou R$ 1,97 milhão em despesas. Cerca de R$ 400 mil (20%) foram destinados ao digital, enquanto os gastos com material gráfico chegaram a aproximadamente R$ 775 mil (39%).

Erika e Sâmia chegaram à eleição com comunidades digitais consolidadas, mas destinaram mais recursos a outras formas de comunicação.

Para Chicarino, seguidores podem representar um tipo de capital político, mas o número bruto não basta. Mais importante que a quantidade de seguidores, segundo ela, é o que essa audiência faz com o conteúdo que recebe.

“Ter milhões de seguidores é um ativo? Claro que é, né? E aí a gente está falando de capital digital. Um capital político digital. Mas ter milhões de seguidores não significa que você vai ter milhões de votos", diz.

“O que importa é o engajamento, é a circulação. Porque, mesmo quando a pessoa compartilha uma coisa para criticar, você está dando tracionamento algorítmico para aquilo.”

Paulo Faltay, professor de Comunicação no Campus do Agreste da Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE) e coordenador do Estopim — Laboratório de Tecnopolítica, Comunicação e Subjetividade, afirma que as plataformas mudaram não apenas os canais usados pelos políticos, mas a própria circulação da informação.

“As diferentes arquiteturas das plataformas, as métricas, os valores, o que é valorizado estão ali definindo que tipo de conteúdo vai ter mais visibilidade, que tipo de conteúdo vai ter mais circulação", diz.

Isso faz com que cada plataforma imponha formatos e estratégias próprios e transforme o próprio público em parte da circulação política.

“O grande feito de ter milhões de seguidores é justamente poder contar com essa audiência que não é apenas destinatário da comunicação, mas passa a trabalhar na própria produção de visibilidade do candidato.”

Em vez de pensar apenas em seguidores, Faltay considera mais importante a existência de uma comunidade que acompanha o político e participa de sua presença pública.

“A questão aqui é muito mais a capacidade de mobilização e como essa capacidade de mobilização tá articulada com as infraestruturas das plataformas e as formas de circulação política delas", diz.

O efeito é uma fragmentação maior da experiência política. Ou seja, diferentes grupos podem ser expostos a conteúdos e referências diferentes, e as campanhas passam a adaptar suas mensagens a essas comunidades.

“Plataformas e redes sociais apresentam o mundo visível e o mundo informacional personalizado para cada pessoa.”

Os outros dois candidatos do levantamento também mostram que não existe uma relação automática entre audiência digital, dinheiro investido e votação.

Kim Kataguiri (Missão) recebeu 520.071 votos e declarou R$ 469 mil em despesas. Cerca de R$ 118 mil (25%) foram destinados ao digital, enquanto aproximadamente R$ 116 mil (25%) foram gastos com material gráfico e postagem.

Eduardo Suplicy (PT), de 85 anos, recebeu 654.627 votos e declarou R$ 97,8 mil em despesas. Cerca de R$ 30 mil (31%) foram destinados ao digital.

Para Faltay, a desigualdade entre as campanhas também passa pela capacidade financeira de cada candidato de explorar as plataformas e adaptar sua comunicação ao funcionamento delas.

“Não é simplesmente quem pode se comunicar melhor, mas é quem se adapta melhor às próprias métricas e arquitetura das plataformas e quem tem mais poder econômico para gastar nelas também.”

articles.title: Map of Middle East redrawn after October 7
articles.summary: Three years of war have upended alliances, weakened US influence and reshaped the region’s power balance.
articles.body:
In the past three years, following the October 7 attacks and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, the wider region has been marked by conflict, economic turmoil, and a shattering of the balance of power.

The network of alliances maintained by Iran, long central to its regional power, has been hit hard and severely weakened. Yemen’s Houthi rebels remain one notable exception.

Israel has made gains. Many of the leaders of the Lebanese group Hezbollah and the Palestinian group Hamas have been killed, while Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was also assassinated in February. Israel occupies most of Gaza, where it has also killed more than 74,000 Palestinians and reduced much of the enclave to rubble.

Its military aggression has come at a cost, isolating it from its traditional allies and making it globally unpopular, including in the United States. The potential for more normalisation deals with Arab countries seems unlikely, at least in the short term.

Instead, Israel continues to launch attacks across the region, crossing previously held red lines – such as the 2025 attack on Doha, Qatar – and making many governments around the world view it as the primary source of unrest in the Middle East.

“Before October 7, the US’s entire policy in the Middle East rested on normalising Israel’s presence in the region through its so-called Abraham Accords,” HA Hellyer of the Royal United Services Institute said, referring to the normalisation deals with several Arab states, including the United Arab Emirates. “Israel’s response to the October 7 attack ended that.”

Instead, rather than a stable Middle East with Israel at its centre, the US entered into a war with Iran this year, and has since looked on as Tehran targeted US allies across the Gulf, shattering the perceived security of the US security umbrella.

Drones and missiles hit Qatar’s Ras Laffan gas hub and started fires near Dubai airport and at Fujairah’s oil zone. In September, the Houthis surged down Yemen’s Red Sea coast, taking the port of Mocha and nearby islands. Their gains tightened their grip on the Bab al-Mandeb strait, threatening a key route for global trade and energy supplies that had become even more important amid disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

“There’s been a loss of faith in the US as a singularly sufficient security guarantor,” Hellyer continued.

“This is why you’re seeing many in the region talk to other external actors, in addition to continuing, and in some cases deepening their US ties, as well as initiatives such as the Mecca security pact as states in the region look elsewhere for ways to safeguard their security,” he said, referring to the defence agreement between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan, signed in August, agreeing that an attack on one was to be regarded as an attack on all.

Alongside the loss of confidence in the US as a security guarantor has come a dramatic reordering of alliances and rivalries. Much of Iran’s network – most notably Hezbollah, whose reputation had long served as a deterrent against Israeli attack – appeared to buckle under Israeli pressure.

That, in turn, emboldened an Israeli military push that saw troops invade Lebanon in October 2024 and again in March 2026 , and seize Syrian territory during the brief power vacuum that followed Bashar al-Assad’s ouster in 2024 .

“The Middle East has always been multi-aligned. However, now it’s even more so,” Sanam Vakil, the director of the Middle East and North Africa Programme at Chatham House, said of the increased leverage given to external actors, such as Turkiye in Syria and China’s involvement in negotiations over the end to war on Iran, as Beijing finds its own energy supplies under threat.

“It’s ironic, since October 7, it’s Israel that has emerged as the revisionist power and Iran almost as the status quo power,” she said of the apparent reversal in status of the two belligerents, with Tehran seemingly more focused on regaining the ground it has lost in the last three years rather than advancing beyond them.

However, none of this was to overstate Israeli influence, or liken it to a regional superpower, Vakil cautioned. “Israel may currently be the preponderant military power in the Middle East, but real power is typically classed as being able to project stability, which Israel hasn’t shown itself able or willing to do,” she said.

While Israel and the US hoped February’s attacks would swiftly topple Iran’s government, they have instead opened a new front. Tehran now wields economic leverage over Israel, the US and their partners through the Strait of Hormuz, which borders Iran and typically carries about a fifth of the world’s oil and gas, and through Bab al-Mandeb, which is now threatened by its Houthi allies.

Whatever Tehran’s intentions, the economic pain has been uneven. The West, cushioned by emergency reserves, record US oil production and supplies from countries such as Norway, has so far avoided the turmoil of the 1970s oil shocks, when US drivers queued for petrol, even though the current disruption is on a greater scale. In April, the International Monetary Fund trimmed its 2026 global growth forecast only slightly, to 3.1 percent from 3.3 percent.

Gulf exporters, in contrast, have fared far worse. The same assessment cut its forecast for Saudi Arabia from 4.5 to 3.1 percent, and turned Qatar’s from growth of 6.1 percent into a contraction of 8.6 percent.

“It’s curious, in many ways the West’s reduced need for Gulf oil has increased the degree to which Israel has become a liability for the US,” Israeli political economist Shir Hever told Al Jazeera, referring to a diplomatic alliance between the two states long underpinned by Israel’s strategic position in an oil-rich region central to US interests.

“There’s a train of thought in Israel that the current crises may push the Gulf states into allying with it,” he said, while noting the irony that Israel had been the main aggressor in the conflicts that followed October 7. “Though that seems fairly unlikely.”

articles.title: Sam Wood: Former Bachelor Australia star denied bail over domestic violence charges
articles.summary: The fitness coach is accused of strangling and assaulting a woman while on holiday in Queensland.
articles.body:
Former Bachelor Australia star and fitness coach Sam Wood will remain in jail after he was denied bail over alleged domestic violence offences.

Wood was arrested on Saturday at a beachfront property on Queensland's Sunshine Coast, and later charged with domestic violence assault and strangulation.

His lawyer told the court on Thursday Wood may argue he acted in self defence during a family fight, but stressed he denies the strangulation charge.

The 46-year-old rose to fame in the 2015 season of the reality TV show and later became the public face of a popular online home fitness and nutrition brand, 28 by Sam Wood - from which he was dumped after his arrest.

Wood - who lives in Melbourne but was on holiday in Noosa - appeared via videolink at Maroochydore Magistrates Court where he applied for bail after five nights in custody.

Police prosecutors told the court the alleged victim had provided a video statement in which she said she had been choked, couldn't breathe, and had her head banged against the floor.

"She thought she was going to die," Sergeant Jeanette Grigoris said.

They also tendered photos of the alleged victim's injuries, as well as a recording of a call to emergency services in which a witness says the woman was choked.

The complainant supports the criminal charges, Grigoris added.

Wood's lawyer Mathew Cuskelly had argued that there was a lack of evidence to support the strangulation charge, which "seems unusual" given the "nature" and "gravity" of the allegation.

He also said his client had been involved in an argument, in which the complainant had been "hostile" when he pushed her - circumstances which could entitle him to a self-defence claim.

Cuskelly said Wood suffers from severe depression, and argued he should be bailed so that he can access mental health support and salvage his professional reputation "which has taken a hell of a beating".

But Grigoris argued there was a risk Wood would interfere with witnesses or reoffend, or fail to return to Queensland to face court.

On Monday, a statement "from the Wood family" was released on both he and his wife's social media.

"This is a difficult time for all of us, we are working through this as a family and thoroughly co-operating with the authorities," the post said.

DBG Health, which bought Wood's fitness brand for millions of dollars in 2022, initially said Wood had been placed on "indefinite leave" but later announced it had cut its commercial arrangements with him "effective immediately".

"DGB Health does not tolerate domestic violence in any form, and our thoughts are with people impacted by it," the company said.

Since the charges, a number of fitness influencers and corporate sponsors have also cut ties with Wood including fitness trainer Tiffiny Hall and Married At First Sight star Jules Robinson.

Wood came to national prominence during the 2015 season of The Bachelor Australia where he met contestant Snezana Markoski.

They married in 2018 and have four daughters, including one from his wife's former relationship.

Wood is next due in court on 23 November.

articles.title: Yemen’s government needs tribes to defeat the Houthis. Will they join?
articles.summary: Yemen’s tribes could prove crucial to government’s fight against the Houthis, but many may wait before choosing sides.
articles.body:
Sanaa, Yemen – The Yemeni government’s new military offensive against the Houthis is testing more than the balance of forces in the country – it is also testing whether the government can persuade powerful tribes in Houthi-controlled areas that the balance of power is beginning to shift.

For years, many of the tribes hostile or wary of the Iran-backed Houthis have stopped short of openly confronting the movement, deterred by their military strength and by previous failed uprisings. Those same tribes are now looking to the internationally recognised government’s newly-activated frontlines – on the Red Sea coast, Marib and al-Jawf primarily – to see if the limited advances made since the Dawn of Yemen military operation launch this week can turn into sustained gains .

The offensive by the Saudi Arabia-backed government forces follows major Houthi gains in September, when the armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God) swept across the country’s Red Sea coast. The Houthis captured vital trade corridors, including the port city of Mocha and territory around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, one of the world’s most important shipping routes.

While airstrikes have inflicted losses on Houthi forces over the past few days, pushing towards Houthi strongholds where the group has been entrenched since the war started in 2014, including Sanaa, Saada, and Amran, remains a formidable challenge.

With the government declaring an all-out war on the Houthis, pledging to recapture Sanaa, tribal distrust of the government may diminish, prompting tribes to shift positions at the right time, experts say. The role of the tribes could therefore prove critical to the government’s ability to advance deeper into Houthi-controlled territories.

On Monday, Marib governorate – the government’s stronghold in the north – saw a large tribal rally attended by tribal sheikhs and local anti-Houthi fighters from tribes such as the Jadan from Marib, Nihm from Sanaa and other allied tribes.

The rally announced a general mobilisation to support the armed forces in the battle to “restore the state and topple the Houthi coup”.

“If this tribal support translates into actual mobilisation and sustained participation in the battle, tribes will help government troops advance toward Houthi-controlled areas and the Houthi heartland, including Sanaa,” said Adel Dashela, a researcher at the Sana’a Center for Strategic Studies.

Over the past decade of war in Yemen, tribes have repeatedly mobilised against the Houthis at a local level, but deep divisions and a lack of sustained outside backing have prevented the emergence of a unified tribal front. Nevertheless, tribes can potentially be a key source of manpower and influence for the government.

“Tribal fighters remain indispensable to any future campaign against the Houthis. But to be effective, their military engagement must occur through formalised state and coalition command structures, rather than as an independent vanguard,” Dashela said.

Tribes in Yemen do not want to risk confronting Houthi forces without support, and they “wait for the right time” to act, Abdulsalam Mohammed, chairman of the Yemeni Abaad Studies and Research Center, said.

“The tribes seek a powerful state, and once they find the state reliable, they can side with it,” Mohammed said.

He added that tribes do not want to repeat mistakes made by tribes that had rebelled against the Houthis, and then not received enough support from the government.

“Those tribes revolted against the Houthis, and they were crushed amid the absence of the government’s effective role,” Mohammed said.

In January 2019, fighting broke out between the Houthis and the Hajoor tribe in northwest Yemen’s Hajjah, lasting several weeks. The Houthis eventually captured the Hajoor areas in March of the same year.

At the time, Saudi Arabia dropped food, medical supplies and weapons to besieged Hajoor fighters, but this did not prevent the tribe’s defeat by the Houthis.

Mohammed said that even in areas where the Houthis have local support, some tribes could gradually shift their allegiance towards the government, if they saw it as serving their interest.

“Not all tribes fighting for the Houthis are staunch supporters. Their motivations range from pragmatism to ideological loyalty and material necessity,” Mohammed said.

Over the past decade, the Houthis have weakened traditional tribal power structures in areas under their control, co-opting some leaders and replacing others with loyalists. They have defeated tribal challenges, and have withstood not only conflict with the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia, but also bombing by the United States, the United Kingdom and Israel. All of that has reinforced a perception among tribes that the Houthi military capability had become “invincible”.

A tribal sheikh in northern Yemen, who asked not to be named for security reasons, told Al Jazeera that the Houthi military “supremacy” in the country over a decade-long war has “dwarfed the political and military role of the tribe”.

“Before the Houthi takeover of power, the government was like a friend of the tribe,” he said. “Today, the tribe is subordinate to the Houthis.”

The Houthis, according to him, used three tactics to tighten their grip on territories under their control: military force, financial incentives and their public identification with the Palestinian cause.

“The Houthis used military force if negotiations or financial incentives failed to win the tribes’ backing. Moreover, the Houthi military support for Palestine has earned the group additional popular and tribal support,” said the tribal figure.

As the Houthis built up enormous military and financial power over the past few years, the tribal sheikh said tribes acting alone could not match the group’s power. He also said that the government’s reported gains on some frontlines could not by themselves be taken as a sign that the Houthis were collapsing.

“A concrete government advance on the battlefields would reassure some Yemeni tribes that the Houthis have lost ground,” the tribal sheikh said. “Once this materialises, anti-Houthi and neutral tribes can feel confident and begin confronting the group.”

articles.title: Teddy Young: Royal Navy sailor in court accused of preparing to spy for Russia
articles.summary: The 24-year-old man appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Thursday after being arrested at his home in Bedfordshire.
articles.body:
A junior Royal Navy sailor accused of preparing to spy for Russia has appeared in court.

Able Seaman Teddy Young, who specialised in warfare intelligence, allegedly retained UK defence and intelligence material that he had access to and made preparations to disclose sensitive information, a court was told.

The 24-year-old appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Thursday after being charged under the National Security Act.

The BBC understands that the allegations against Young include translating a message into Russian and looking for a web portal that invited people to submit information to Russia.

Wearing a police-issue grey sweatshirt, Young spoke in court to confirm his name, date of birth and his address in Clapham, near Bedford.

He is formally charged with engaging in conduct in preparation for disclosing protected information, and obtaining, copying, recording or retaining protected information, intending the conduct to benefit a foreign power.

The charges cover a period between 26 November 2024 and 21 May 2025.

"The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power," the Crown Prosecution Service told the court in a written summary of the allegations.

Police said the alleged offences were not related to the recent RAF Fairford incident that resulted in a number of arrests after suspicious activity was reported near the base.

In total, seven men have been arrested and later released on bail in connection with the incident, which is being investigated by counter-terror police.

Young was arrested at his home address in Bedfordshire on Tuesday.

He is the first member of the armed forces to be charged under the new National Security Act 2023.

Cdr Helen Flanagan, head of Counter Terrorism Policing London, said: "These are very serious charges against a serving member of the armed forces.

"We have worked extremely closely with relevant operational colleagues within the Ministry of Defence as our investigation has progressed to ensure appropriate measures could be taken to mitigate any potential risks linked to this matter."

A Royal Navy spokesperson confirmed a service member had been charged and added: "As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage."

Judge Annabel Pilling remanded Young in custody. He will next appear at the Old Bailey on 16 October.

articles.title: U.K. rebrands east Jerusalem consulate after Israel orders closure
articles.summary: Britain said on Thursday its nearly 200-year-old consulate in Jerusalem would remain operating at a smaller scale, renamed as the “UK Mission” in the city, after Israel ordered ​it shut in a dispute over sanctions on settlements.
articles.body: JERUSALEM — Britain said on Thursday its nearly 200-year-old consulate in Jerusalem would remain operating at a smaller scale, renamed as the “UK Mission” in the city, after Israel ordered ​it shut in a dispute over sanctions on settlements. Israel last month issued a 30-day deadline for ‌Britain to close the consulate after London announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a dispute that has strained relations between the longtime allies. The deadline expired on Thursday. Gideon Saar, Israel’s foreign minister, said in a statement that the consulate, in east Jerusalem, would ​formally end operations but that some British diplomats would be allowed to continue work in the building under ​a deal struck between Israel and Britain. Saar’s British counterpart, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, said his ⁠country does not accept that Israel has the legal right to close the consulate. The consulate is in a ​part of the city Israel captured in a 1967 war, which Israel later annexed in a move that most countries do ​not recognize. Miliband said that following discussions with Israel, “our Consulate General building will not be closing, and will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem from today.” Miliband said the UK Mission would continue to “deliver vital services and our work with the Palestinian people.” Earlier on Thursday, Reuters journalists saw workers in the consulate remove a plaque reading “British Consulate General” and another sign for its ​consular section. The British flag was still flying over the building. Israel last month ordered Britain to close the consulate within 30 days and ‌remove its ⁠diplomats from the city, after Britain announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, including a trade ban on goods made there. The United Nations and most countries consider the Israeli settlements to be illegal under international law. Israel disputes this. Israel has been adamant the consulate will close even as Britain sought to keep it open, including sending the country’s top ​national security adviser to Israel ​last week for talks. Britain’s consulate ⁠was founded in 1839, long before the State of Israel was established in 1948. The closure order does not affect Britain’s embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with ​Israel’s government. The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighborhood of east Jerusalem, handles Britain’s relations with ​Palestinians in ⁠Jerusalem, as well as in the West Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians. The British sanctions announcement, and Israel’s order to close the consulate, mark a new low in a relationship that has deteriorated over the past three years. ⁠Britain has ​repeatedly criticized Israel over its actions in the war in Gaza and ​over Israeli settler attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, which faces an election later this month, has accused Britain’s governing Labour ​Party of being hostile towards Israel.

articles.title: ‘South Mumbai clean doesn’t mean entire city is clean’: Bombay HC questions BMC over Mumbai’s garbage woes
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday pulled up the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) over waste management and cleanliness in Mumbai,
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Bombay high court on Wednesday pulled up the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) over waste management and cleanliness in Mumbai, observing that the city could not be considered clean merely because some parts of South Mumbai were well maintained.“Everywhere there is filth… Only because Worli is clean or South Mumbai is clean, or Nariman Point is clean, that doesn’t mean entire Mumbai is clean,” a bench of Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale said orally.The bench was hearing a petition filed by residents of Kannamwar Nagar over the Kanjurmarg waste management facility and concerns about its impact on the health of residents in nearby areas.BMC senior advocate Anil Sakhare submitted that the situation had improved. The HC, however, said it did not find “very high progress” by BMC ward officers in addressing problematic areas concerning health and hygiene at public places, hill slopes, pavements and streets.The court directed the BMC to file a comprehensive affidavit detailing the steps taken by ward officers to ascertain the “correct position” on the ground and the measures undertaken on Gandhi Jayanti as part of the Swachhata Abhiyan. The bench also warned that ward officers could be called to court to explain the situation.The judges said they had noticed a heap of plastic near a municipal school in Jogeshwari. “Can we believe that this is Mumbai? Simple cleaning will take no more than one day. Nothing has happened. It is unbelievable,” Justice Kulkarni said.Residents of Vikhroli and environmental NGO Vanashakti have also raised concerns over rampant dumping of garbage along roadsides and in water bodies.Justice Kulkarni, referring to the role of citizens in keeping the city clean, said people followed rules and refrained from littering when they travelled abroad because there were deterrents and cameras, but “here there is absolutely no worry”.The bench said that once the system was put in place and citizens were sensitised, people would eventually stop throwing garbage on the streets. “We are looking at Mumbai to be converted into that kind of city where people themselves will go and throw everything in the dustbin,” it said.BMC lists measures takenIn its detailed affidavit filed before the HC on Wednesday by Sakhare to show compliance, the BMC said it had held a meeting in August pursuant to earlier court directions to discuss issues relating to the Kanjurmarg facility, compliance with HC directions and measures to ensure effective monitoring.The civic body said mitigation of odour and other forms of pollution at the facility were being monitored by a committee, as reflected in the minutes of the meeting.The BMC also said it had acted on several issues flagged by the HC earlier.It said a compactor located at a heritage site had been shifted out, while the location of a chowki opposite the City Civil Court and the route and parking arrangements for garbage vehicles near the heritage building had also been addressed by shifting the garbage vehicles’ reporting point away from the court.On ward-level garbage collection, the BMC said it had placed on record a ward-level structure for collection.On illegal dumping in public areas, the civic body said it had prepared an action plan, identified garbage-vulnerable points (GVPs), installed CCTV cameras to monitor them and taken action against people found illegally dumping or littering, including by imposing fines under BMC bye-laws.The BMC also said it had undertaken public-awareness initiatives on responsible garbage disposal, including an appeal by the municipal commissioner to elected representatives to sensitise articles.title: FBI says it stopped a Mall of America terror attack by a teen after agents sold him an assault rifle
articles.summary: FBI agents thwarted a terror attack by a teenager on the Mall of America after monitoring him for nearly two years and ultimately supplying him with the AK-47 he planned to use, authorities said Wednesday.
articles.body: MINNEAPOLIS — FBI agents thwarted a terror attack by a teenager on the Mall of America after monitoring him for nearly two years and ultimately supplying him with the AK-47 he planned to use, authorities said Wednesday. The 18-year-old had been on the FBI’s radar since December 2024, when he began trading messages with a confidential informant. A criminal complaint says he initially expressed an interest in traveling to Somalia to fight for al-Shabab militants. As his plans to instead attack the mall solidified, the complaint says, agents sold him the gun and ammunition on Tuesday and arrested him on the spot. “This was a radicalized young man who needed to be watched,” U.S. Attorney Daniel Rosen said. Agents “were able to detect a threat, and disrupt it, before the defendant carried out his intention to kill, in his words, maybe 30 to 60 people.” Sheikhdoon Abdullahi Mohamud was arrested Tuesday in a public park in Richfield, several miles northwest of the Mall of America, after he paid $600 to an undercover FBI employee posing as a member of the Islamic State group for the rifle and 200 rounds of ammunition, the agency said. Mohamud appeared in a yellow jail uniform for his initial appearance Wednesday in federal court in St. Paul. He told the judge he did not have a job, own a house or a car, or have any money in the bank. He was represented by Siri Carlson McDowell, a federal public defender. Carlson McDowell and relatives of Mohamud declined to comment after the hearing. Rosen said Mohamud is an American-born U.S. citizen of Somali descent. According to an FBI agent’s sworn complaint, Mohamud repeatedly affirmed in chat messages to the informant that he intended to attack and kill non-Muslims at the mall on Oct. 24, the date of a scheduled arts celebration by the Hmong community, Minnesota’s largest Asian ethnic group. When the informant asked if he was serious about committing the attack, Mohamud replied, “yes i am 100% sure,” the complaint said, and added: “I would have backed out by now if I wasn’t sure.” The agent wrote that Mohamud’s messages expressed admiration for recent terror attacks as well as an interest in traveling to fight in Somalia, ultimately for the Islamic State group. He later decided he couldn’t afford to travel there and would attack the mall instead, the complaint said. The teen first came to the FBI’s attention in December 2024, the same month the source began exchanging messages with him, the complaint said. By May 2025, agents were concerned enough that they went to his home. His mother told them he wasn’t home from school yet and called the boy’s father, who declined to speak with them and said he would give their contact information to his lawyer, the complaint said. “What I would say to parents all over Minnesota, and all over America: If you get any indication — especially if you hear from federal law enforcement — that your son or daughter is being radicalized, to the point where federal law enforcement wants to come and give you that warning, those are warnings that ought to be heeded,” Rosen said. Tens of thousands of people of Somali descent live in Minnesota, dating back to when refugees began arriving in the 1990s. Over the years several have been charged with attempting to join militant groups.

articles.title: Wife of ex-Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro seeks release from U.S. jail
articles.summary: The wife of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is set to be back in court Thursday, where her lawyers will urge a judge to free her from jail and put her under house arrest due to ongoing heart problems.
articles.body: NEW YORK — The wife of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro is set to be back in court Thursday, where her lawyers will urge a judge to free her from jail and put her under house arrest due to ongoing heart problems. Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores have been behind bars in New York since early January when forces seized them from their Caracas home in a middle-of-the-night raid. Both have pleaded not guilty in a criminal case first brought six years ago against them and numerous alleged co-conspirators. They face potential life prison sentences if convicted of being part of a conspiracy to send cocaine into the U.S. Their attorneys have asked for the case to be dismissed on the grounds that they have immunity as the leader and first lady of a foreign country. Lawyers for Flores, 69, have also argued that she has medical issues that cannot be treated effectively in jail, and that she could instead be allowed to live under 24-hour guard at a residence in New York. They also said she suffered permanent scarring when she was “thrown against a wall or dresser” during the U.S. military action that led to her capture. Her lawyers say she has lost 25 pounds while imprisoned at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn and has been told that she might need heart surgery. They said she also suffers from “lingering lightheadedness, dizziness and shortness of breath” and might have suffered a minor heart attack in July. Prosecutors opposed the bail request. In a court filing, they wrote that Flores would pose an “extreme risk of flight and danger to the public” if released. They also said she has been taken from the jail to get treatment at a local hospital, when care was needed. President Donald Trump’s administration has defended the raid to capture Maduro as a “surgical law enforcement operation.” Maduro has called himself a prisoner of war and his capture a kidnapping. Flores is charged with participating in a cocaine importation conspiracy with her husband, Maduro, who served as Venezuela’s president from 2013 until his capture by American forces in January. Lawyers for Flores said she was no threat to flee because she is “intent on supporting her husband with her constant presence.”

articles.title: India defends satellite internet approval process after Elon Musk jab
articles.summary: Musk has claimed unnamed entities are blocking Starlink’s launch to maintain their monopoly.
articles.body:
India has refuted billionaire Elon Musk’s claim that “certain oligarchs” are blocking the launch of his Starlink satellite communication services in the country.

Musk said in an X post on Wednesday that Starlink was being blocked so that unnamed individuals can “maintain their monopolistic chokehold on the Indian people”, adding that it was a “crime against the people of India”.

But India’s Ministry of Communications defended its satellite internet approval process as being fair and non-discriminatory in a statement on Thursday.

“The suggestion that the framework or its application is unfair or discriminatory is baseless and misconceived,” the ministry said without naming Starlink or Musk.

It added that three different entities were at broadly the same regulatory stage and that all were undergoing security assessments.

India’s telecommunications sector is dominated by Reliance Jio, owned by billionaire Mukesh Ambani, and Bharti Airtel, owned by Sunil Mittal.

Both have also ventured into satellite internet. While they have secured early approvals to launch, they are still awaiting final clearances.

Musk has previously had run-ins with Ambani and Mittal over how India should grant them spectrum access. Last year, the two agreed to distribute Starlink systems alongside theirs, but the cooperation appears to have soured.

Starlink has waited since 2022 for licences to operate commercially in India. Last year, it received a key licence from the Communications Ministry to launch, as well as a go-ahead from India’s space agency.

Concerns over security have mounted since 2024 after authorities said they found Starlink devices in a drug seizure operation in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, as well as in another army operation in Manipur state.

At the time, Musk alleged Starlink’s satellite beams were thereafter “turned off over India” and that they were “never on in the first place”.

articles.title: Missouri sued over alleged decades of underfunding at historically Black university
articles.summary: Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state, alleging it violated ‌the U.S. Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades.
articles.body: CHICAGO — Seven current and former students at Lincoln University of Missouri sued the state on Wednesday, alleging it violated ‌the U.S. Constitution and federal civil rights law by systematically underfunding the historically Black university for decades. The complaint, filed in federal court in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Missouri Central Division, seeks compensatory damages under Title VI of the Civil Rights Act for what plaintiffs describe as “educational ​and economic injuries” caused by decades of underfunding. It also seeks an injunction requiring Missouri to fully match Lincoln University’s ​federal land-grant funding in the future. Some of the funding they are requesting would include campus repairs, faculty ⁠hiring, student services, financial aid and agricultural research programs. Lincoln University, in Jefferson City, is the state’s first historically Black land-grant institution. ​The University of Missouri is the state’s predominantly white land-grant institution. The plaintiffs allege Missouri appropriated less per student to Lincoln than to ​the University of Missouri in most fiscal years between 1987 and 2020. They cited a September 2023 letter in which the U.S. agriculture and education secretaries calculated that Missouri had underfunded Lincoln by $361.6 million over that period, based on federal higher education data. According to the complaint, Missouri provided no state matching ​funds for Lincoln’s federal land-grant allocation from fiscal 2000 through 2007, and supplied only a portion of the required match in subsequent ​years. Lincoln allegedly diverted about $43.5 million from its general operating budget between 2000 and 2016 to cover the state’s share, and returned nearly $8 million ‌in federal ⁠funds from 2016 through 2018 when it could not meet matching requirements. Missouri fully matched the University of Missouri’s land-grant allocations during the same period, the complaint said. The University of Missouri declined to comment, citing “ongoing litigation.” Lincoln University of Missouri did not respond to an immediate request for comment. The lawsuit names the State of Missouri, the state Coordinating Board for Higher Education, Governor Michael Kehoe, Higher Education Commissioner ​Bennett Boggs and University of ​Missouri System President Mun Choi ⁠as defendants. State officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit argues the funding gap perpetuates the legacy of Missouri’s formerly segregated higher education system, under which the University of Missouri ​served white students and Lincoln was established for Black students. “Lincoln is constantly putting Band-Aids over bullet ​wounds because they ⁠do not have the resources to fully address the blow,” Makhi Jaff, a plaintiff, said in the lawsuit. Plaintiffs include alumni who attended Lincoln in the 1980s and 1990s, a former student who left without a degree in 2024, and four current students. They describe deteriorating residence halls, ⁠limited dining ​and health services, scarce course offerings, inadequate advising and financial hardship. One student stated ​in the lawsuit that she lost weight because dining services closed before band practice ended. Another student said a scholarship she expected to cover her education was ​withdrawn, requiring her to take loans and work up to 30 hours weekly.

articles.title: Noida road rage caught on dashcam; driver chases commuter, brake-checks car
articles.summary: NOIDA: A suspected road-rage incident in Noida, in which a driver allegedly drove on the wrong side of the road, chased another motorist and then
articles.body: NOIDA: A suspected road-rage incident in Noida, in which a driver allegedly drove on the wrong side of the road, chased another motorist and then brake-checked his car, has gone viral on social media. The incident was captured on a dashboard camera and has triggered concerns over aggressive driving and road safety.The video, shared on X by user Abhishek Jalan, purportedly shows a car travelling on the wrong side of the road near the median before turning around and following another vehicle. The driver allegedly attempts to block the commuter's path by abruptly applying the brakes in front of his car.The footage then shows the driver getting out of his vehicle and approaching the other car. The commuter, however, appears to avoid confrontation. He keeps the doors of his vehicle locked, maintains a safe distance from the other car and waits for an opportunity to move away.Jalan tagged Noida Police and Uttar Pradesh Police while sharing the footage and urged authorities to examine the incident. He also pointed out that the registration number of the vehicle allegedly involved was visible in the video.The post drew attention online, with several users praising the commuter for not getting out of his vehicle or engaging with the other driver. Many also urged police to take action against motorists who resort to aggressive driving and intimidation on city roads.UP Police's 112 emergency service took cognisance of the post. Responding to Jalan on X on Wednesday, the official handle asked him to share his contact number through direct message. It was not immediately clear whether a formal complaint had subsequently been registered or whether any action had been initiated against the driver.The incident has once again highlighted the risks associated with road rage, particularly when drivers respond to minor disagreements with aggressive manoeuvres. Traffic experts and police officials have repeatedly advised motorists not to engage with aggressive drivers, but instead maintain distance, keep vehicle doors locked and move to a safe location.In this case too, the commuter's decision to remain inside the vehicle and drive away rather than confront the alleged aggressor has been widely appreciated on social media.The viral footage comes amid continued enforcement against traffic violations in Noida. articles.title: Gaza war sped up India’s shift towards Israel under Modi
articles.summary: As even Israel’s traditional allies are distancing themselves from Netanyahu, Modi’s India has embraced the country.
articles.body:
New Delhi, India – The United Kingdom, France, Australia, New Zealand, Canada and Norway had already banned the entry of Bezalel Smotrich, Israel’s far-right finance minister, who had advocated the ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in Gaza and the annexation of the occupied West Bank.

But in September 2025, as the European Union was planning bloc-wide sanctions against him and his fellow far-right colleague Itamar Ben-Gvir that it would eventually announce late that month, Smotrich was welcomed with garlands and a multi-city trip to India. In New Delhi, he signed a trade deal; in Mumbai, he visited the stock exchange; and in Gujarat – the home state of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi – he travelled to a new investment hub.

As Israel was conducting its genocidal war on Gaza, bombing and killing dozens on the very days he was visiting India, New Delhi was ready to expand business with Israel like never before. For decades, India had been one of the world’s staunchest supporters of Palestine, and Europe one of Israel’s closest backers. India’s position has shifted firmly since 2014, when Modi and his Hindu majoritarian Bharatiya Janata Party came to power. But analysts say the optics of Smotrich’s visit underlined something even more dramatic: At a time when even Europe, traditionally seen as backing Israel, has veered away from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government, the genocidal war on Gaza appears to have escalated India’s embrace of Israel.

In February this year, Modi visited Israel as Netanyahu – who faces an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court over war crimes carried out in Gaza – faced growing isolation in the international arena.

“You are a great friend of Israel. You are more than a friend. You are a brother,” Netanyahu told Modi when both leaders addressed the Israeli parliament in Jerusalem.

Three years of Israeli attacks have killed at least 74,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,000 children. That is about one in every 30 people, or 3 percent of the pre-war population.

Historically, India has argued that diplomacy and dialogue are the way forward to resolve conflicts – whether between Russia and Ukraine, the US and Iran, or Israel and Palestine. New Delhi has maintained that war doesn’t solve anything.

But investigations by Al Jazeera and other reporting have revealed that New Delhi exported weapons to Israel during the ongoing genocidal war on Gaza. Meanwhile, under Modi, India has become Israel’s largest weapons buyer.

Just hours after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023, India’s Modi unequivocally condemned the “terrorist attack”, adding that he was “deeply shocked”. When he visited Israel in February this year, Modi referred to the Mumbai attacks in 2008, carried out by Pakistani fighters, which New Delhi has blamed on the Pakistani government. “Like you, we have a consistent and uncompromising policy of zero tolerance for terrorism with no double standards,” Modi said.

Analysts believe that the framing of Israel as a country under attack has helped Modi justify pushing India closer to it. For decades, much of the politics of Modi’s BJP “has hovered around Islamist expansionism or Islamic terrorism”, said Rasheed Kidwai, a political analyst in New Delhi.

“So it helps [in relationship with Israel],” Kidwai said, pointing to the link between Modi’s Israel policy and his domestic politics. “Take this relationship as an extension of the domestic narrative that one sees in India.”

The Indian Hindu right has long supported the ideology of Zionism, analysts note. Modi’s BJP has roots in a philosophy, Hindutva, which ultimately seeks to transform India into a Hindu nation and a natural homeland for Hindus anywhere in the world – similar to Israel’s view of itself as a Jewish homeland.

Since the October 7 attacks on Israel, Kidwai noted, “the anti-Muslim sentiments fill in that block in India.” This feeling is, of course, coupled with “pragmatism in New Delhi because Israel is a potent international player”.

Navdeep Suri, a former Indian diplomat who served as ambassador to Egypt and the United Arab Emirates, told Al Jazeera that people-to-people ties are also a central pillar of the India-Israel relationship, “particularly within a section of Indian society that has strong admiration for the muscular policy that Israel adopts”.

Time and again, there have been calls from within Indian right-wing echelons for Modi to adopt more Israel-like policies, from clampdowns in Indian-administered Kashmir to attacking neighbouring Pakistan.

Suri noted that a shift towards Israel predates the ongoing genocidal war in Gaza. “Under PM Modi, a relationship that was largely covert or under the carpet has become a much more open relationship,” the former Indian diplomat said.

“There has been a recognition in Delhi that Israel has been a very strong defence and intelligence partner,” he told Al Jazeera, referring to another pillar of the bilateral relationship. “There’s a genuine convergence when it comes to the perceptions on security.”

India ‘should take principled positions’

Even several of Israel’s closest European allies have moved from criticism of the genocidal war on Gaza and expansive illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank to concrete measures. At least 11 European countries and Canada have imposed trade measures against products from illegal Israeli settlements. Many have imposed sanctions on settlers and networks accused of conducting pogroms against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, as well as on ministers like Smotrich and Ben-Gvir.

India, for its part, has avoided anything more than homilies and mild opposition to war and West Bank attacks.

Diplomatically, New Delhi still backs a two-state solution and has called for aid access and peace in the region. Suri, the former Indian diplomat who served in the Middle East, said New Delhi “should be able to take more principled positions on these things”.

However, from his experience in office, Suri added, “there is such a close alignment at the political levels between the governments in Israel and India that there is a reluctance [in India] to criticise Israel.

“That reluctance manifests in various aspects,” Suri explained to Al Jazeera. “The refusal to criticise the settlers’ attacks; refusal to criticise the brutal use of force in Gaza; refusal to criticise the attack on Iran and point out violation of international norms.”

Unlike Western countries, India’s current leaders “lack that kind of dynamic thinking and are rather far more dogmatic”, said Kidwai, the political analyst.

Netanyahu’s disruptive and fatal assault on Gaza has drawn ire from even the White House in Washington, where Israel enjoys bipartisan support. United States President Donald Trump has previously threatened to cut off support for Israel’s bombing of Lebanon – even while signing off on huge weapons sales to Israel.

However, nothing has moved Modi’s bonhomie with Israel’s Netanyahu.

In fact, Modi’s February visit on the eve of the joint US-Israel attacks on Iran appeared “as almost a personal favour to Netanyahu by boosting his image as an international statesman just as Israeli election campaigning is getting under way”, Max Rodenbeck, Israel/Palestine programme director at the Washington-based International Crisis Group, had told Al Jazeera.

Such an act would have been unthinkable from an Indian leader in previous decades.

In 1948, India opposed the creation of Israel. A relationship with Israel was once frowned upon in New Delhi – a legacy of India’s anti-colonial past – though the two had clandestine ties since at least the 1970s.

India backed the 1975 United Nations General Assembly resolution calling Zionism a form of racism, was the first non-Arab nation to recognise the Palestine Liberation Organization, and was among the first in the world to recognise Palestinian statehood. It only established diplomatic ties with Israel in 1992, and though governments since then slowly built up relations, Modi, in 2016, was the first Indian PM to visit that country.

The Congress party that’s now in opposition, but ruled India for most of its post-independence period before Modi, also viewed its support for Palestine as helpful with Muslim voters – only Indonesia and Pakistan have more Muslims than India – said Kidwai. Modi’s Hindu-first politics, by contrast, thrives on othering Indian Muslims.

“Modi’s party believes it stands to gain nothing from a pro-Palestine posture,” Kidwai told Al Jazeera. “Instead, Modi has sought to link the attack on Israel with the so-called reign of terror and Islamic extremism and make a case against Muslims – and within those realms lies the justification of everything.”
